Prerequisite: A FortiEDR license of one of the three license types (Discover, Protect and Response; Discover and Protect; or Protect and Response), with license seats for the workstations and servers to be protected
What it enables: Collector registration (only the number of Collectors the license allows can register with the Central Manager) and the out-of-the-box security policies (one or all of them, depending on the license); the license type also decides which add-ons are available
How to put it in place: FortiEDR Cloud: register the subscription contract's license activation code in FortiCloud and provision the environment; on premises: send the Installation ID to Fortinet and load the license string that Fortinet returns; GUI: Administration > Licensing (License Type, License Capacity)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Deploying FortiEDR Cloud", "Installing FortiEDR Collectors", "Out-of-the-box policies", "Licensing", and Appendix C, "Configuring the FortiEDR Central Manager server and console" (the licensed entitlements table)

Prerequisite: The Threat Hunting add-on, available with the Discover, Protect and Response or Protect and Response license type, with Repository storage add-ons as needed
What it enables: Threat Hunting, Threat Hunting collection profiles and exclusions, scheduled queries, and the Threat Intelligence Feed queries; Threat Hunting supports only Collectors that run FortiEDR 5.0 or later
How to put it in place: Buy the add-on with the license; GUI: Administration > Licensing (Threat Hunting)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Threat Hunting" (license-dependent add-on), "EDR" (Threat Hunting Settings), Appendix C (licensed entitlements table), and "Step 2 – Defining or importing an organization" (Threat Hunting and Repository storage add-ons)

Prerequisite: The eXtended Detection add-on
What it enables: A working eXtended detection source connector and the eXtended Detection policy (a connector can be created without the license, but the license is required for a successful XDR definition)
How to put it in place: Buy the add-on with the license; GUI: Administration > Licensing (eXtended Detection)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Out-of-the-box policies" (eXtended Detection Policy), "eXtended detection source integration" (Prerequisites of each source), and Appendix C (licensed entitlements table)

Prerequisite: The Communication Control add-on
What it enables: Application communication control
How to put it in place: Buy the add-on with the license; GUI: Administration > Licensing (Communication Control)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, Appendix C, "Configuring the FortiEDR Central Manager server and console" (licensed entitlements table)

Prerequisite: The Vulnerability Management add-on, which comes with the Discover and Protect or Discover, Protect and Response license type
What it enables: The NIST and ACI severity ratings of applications that communication control uses for vulnerability assessment and virtual patching (also Device Control and IoT discovery, which are "No direct requirement" rows)
How to put it in place: Buy a license type that includes the add-on; GUI: Administration > Licensing (Vulnerability Management)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Severity" (ratings only with the Discover and Protect or Discover, Protect and Response license), "Out-of-the-box policies" (Device Control), "IoT devices", and Appendix C (licensed entitlements table)

Prerequisite: The Content Updates add-on
What it enables: Automatic updates of the FortiEDR policy rules and built-in exceptions, and loading content files
How to put it in place: Buy the add-on with the license; GUI: Administration > Licensing (Content Updates)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Protection or Simulation mode" (Content add-on license) and Appendix C (licensed entitlements table)

Prerequisite: On-premises back-end hosts that meet the system requirements: Intel or AMD x86 64-bit virtual machines built from the Fortinet ISO images, with 4 CPUs, 16 GB memory, and 150 GB SSD for the Central Manager; 4 CPUs, 16 GB, and 80 GB for the Aggregator; 4 CPUs, 16 GB, and 250 GB SSD for a Core (2 CPUs, 8 GB, and 50 GB for a Core running as a Jumpbox); 4 CPUs, 16 GB, and 120 GB for the reputation server; and a Threat Hunting Repository sized by seats and data retention
What it enables: Installing, upgrading, and administering the Central Manager, Aggregator, Core, Threat Hunting Repository, and reputation server on premises, including the air-gapped deployment, and assessing each host against its operating system STIG
How to put it in place: Build each VM to the system requirements and set up the components top-down (Central Manager, Aggregator, Threat Hunting Repository, reputation server, Core); fortiedr status
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, Appendix C, "System requirements", "Threat Hunting Repository CPU, Physical Memory, and Disk Space Requirements", and "Setting up FortiEDR components on-premise"; Appendix D for air-gapped environments

Prerequisite: Network paths between the FortiEDR components: Collectors to the Aggregator on port 8081 and to the Core on port 555 (or the custom port), and the other component ports in the on-premises port table, with the 10.42.x.x and 10.43.x.x ranges not used by any device
What it enables: Collector registration and the channels from Collectors to the Aggregator and Core, including the SSL channel between Collector and Core
How to put it in place: Open the documented ports in the firewalls, narrowed to the component addresses; behind a web proxy, allow tunneling from the Collector to the Aggregator on port 8081 and to the Core on port 555
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, Appendix C, "Network ports", and "Requesting and obtaining a Collector installer" (Use System Proxy Settings)

Prerequisite: The device registration password, set when the Central Manager is configured
What it enables: Installing, upgrading, and uninstalling Collectors, and unzipping a custom Collector installer
How to put it in place: Set it in the Device Registration Password fields when you configure the Central Manager, and keep it from endpoint users; GUI: Administration > Settings > Component Authentication
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Component Authentication", "Requesting and obtaining a Collector installer", and Appendix C, "Configuring the FortiEDR Central Manager server and console"

Prerequisite: Endpoints whose operating system meets the Collector System Requirements (Windows, macOS, and Linux; Android and iOS through the mobile Collector), with the Collector version that a feature needs: 5.0 or later for Threat Hunting, 6.1 or later for host firewall policies, and 6.2 or later for the Security Content Update (AV signature) and Collector Settings policies and the High-Sensitivity Mode of the File Encryptor rule (Windows)
What it enables: Installing the Collector (Linux Collectors need network access to their package repositories for dependencies, and macOS Collectors need the System Extensions, Network Extensions, and Full Disk Access approvals) and the features that need a minimum Collector version
How to put it in place: Check each endpoint's operating system and Collector version before you assign the feature; GUI: Assets > Inventory
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Installing FortiEDR Collectors" (Collector System Requirements; Windows, macOS, and Linux sections), "Threat Hunting", "Host Firewall", "Security Content Update", "Collector Settings", and "Out-of-the-box policies" (Ransomware Prevention)

Prerequisite: A Core with Jumpbox functionality that has connectivity to the LDAP server or the external system (an on-premises Core; a cloud Core is configured as a Jumpbox only by Fortinet Support)
What it enables: LDAP authentication and the connectors (firewall, NAC, sandbox, eXtended detection sources, custom, Identity Management, and User Access)
How to put it in place: Install an on-premises Core (Setting up the FortiEDR Core) and give it Jumpbox functionality; GUI: Administration > Deployment > System Components (Functionality: Jumpbox)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "LDAP authentication", "System Components" (Cores, Functionality), and the prerequisites of each connector in "Integrations"

Prerequisite: Connectivity from the Central Manager to the FortiEDR Cloud Service (FCS) and the Fortinet cloud destinations of the port table (FCS at rbq.cldsrv.ensilo.com and cldsrv.ensilo.com, AV signature updates at fortiav.cloud.ensilo.com), through the web proxy if one is used
What it enables: The Connectors menu (available only when the environment is connected to FCS) and AV signature updates
How to put it in place: fortiedr config (answer Yes at the Do you want to enable FCS? prompt when installing the Central Manager on premises, and enable the web proxy there if one is needed); Allow those destinations in the firewall
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Integrations" (Connectors menu and FCS), the prerequisites of each connector, and Appendix C, "Setting up a VM to be the FortiEDR Central Manager" and "Network ports"

Prerequisite: Certificates from a DoD-approved CA: a PEM server certificate with its private key whose CN matches the Central Manager FQDN registered in DNS, the approved CA certificates, a certificate for the on-premises Grafana connection, and a client certificate for a TLS syslog server that requires one (for FortiAnalyzer, the client certificate files come from Fortinet Support)
What it enables: HTTPS to the Central Manager console with a trusted certificate, trusted CAs, TLS syslog with a client certificate, and HTTPS for Grafana
How to put it in place: Request the certificates from the DoD PKI, register the Central Manager FQDN in DNS, and on premises set the FQDN in the application-customer.properties file when you load the server certificate
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Loading a server certificate", "Syslog" (TLS and Client Certificate), and Appendix C, "Configuring the FortiEDR Central Manager server and console" (MITM CA certificate); this chapter, Grafana row

Prerequisite: An authoritative time source (NTP server) that the on-premises hosts synchronize with
What it enables: Accurate time stamps on the Central Manager, Aggregator, and Core, whose date and time are otherwise only set at installation
How to put it in place: Configure time synchronization on each Ubuntu host as the Ubuntu STIG requires; FortiEDR Cloud relies on Fortinet's service
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, Appendix C (date, time, and time zone prompts of the installers); this chapter, "Where the commands come from" (Time)

Prerequisite: An SMTP server that accepts mail from the Central Manager
What it enables: Email for security events and system events through distribution lists and playbooks (SMTP must be configured before distribution lists are used)
How to put it in place: Provide the server and its settings, then set and test it; GUI: Profiles > Export settings > SMTP (Test)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "SMTP", "Distribution lists", and "System events"

Prerequisite: A syslog server or SIEM that is reachable from the Central Manager (the source of all syslog messages) over TCP with TLS: FortiAnalyzer for the FAZ format (not FortiAnalyzer Cloud), or a server that accepts the CEF, LEEF, or semicolon format
What it enables: Sending security events, system events, and the audit trail through syslog, and the syslog playbook action
How to put it in place: Set up the server to listen on TCP with TLS; GUI: Profiles > Export settings > Syslog (Test)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Syslog"; FortiEDR 7.2 Syslog Message Reference

Prerequisite: An Active Directory or OpenLDAP directory reachable from the Jumpbox (P11), with a bind user and the directory groups to map to FortiEDR roles (user names without a backslash)
What it enables: LDAP authentication of console users and the mapping of directory groups to the Admin, Senior Analyst, Analyst, IT, and Read-Only roles
How to put it in place: Create the bind user and the groups in the directory; GUI: Administration > Users > LDAP authentication (Directory Type, Bind User DN/Bind Password)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "LDAP authentication"

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider (such as FortiAuthenticator, Okta, or Azure, which may need a Microsoft license for SAML) that has the FortiEDR SP metadata, sends a group attribute in its assertion, and for DoD enforces CAC
What it enables: SAML authentication of console users and the mapping of IdP groups to FortiEDR roles
How to put it in place: Upload the FortiEDR SP metadata to the IdP and define the group attribute; GUI: Administration > Users > SAML authentication (IDP Metadata, Attribute Name)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "SAML authentication" (and the Azure, Okta, and FortiAuthenticator examples)

Prerequisite: FortiToken or a third-party authentication application (such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Okta, or Duo) on each user's mobile device
What it enables: Two-factor authentication for specific users or for all users (Require 2FA)
How to put it in place: Give each user FortiToken or an approved authenticator application before 2FA is required
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Two-factor authentication"

Prerequisite: The external system of each connector, reachable from the Jumpbox, with an API user or token on it: a firewall or FortiManager, FortiNAC or another NAC system, FortiSandbox (an administrator with JSON API access), FortiClient EMS (an API user on premises, or the FortiCloud master user for FortiClient EMS Cloud), Active Directory for User Access, or the third-party system of a custom connector
What it enables: Firewall, NAC, sandbox, Identity Management (FortiClient EMS Zero Trust tagging), User Access, and custom connectors and their playbook actions
How to put it in place: Create the API user or token on the external system; GUI: Profiles > Integrations > Connectors (Host, Port)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Firewall integration", "Network Access Control (NAC) integration", "Sandbox integration", "Custom integration", "Identity Management integration", and "User Access integration" (Prerequisites)

Prerequisite: On the FortiGate (or through FortiManager), an address group for FortiEDR to populate and a firewall policy that denies traffic to the addresses in it
What it enables: Blocking malicious addresses on the firewall with the Block address on Firewall action
How to put it in place: Create the address group and the deny policy on the FortiGate, in the VDOM that the connector names
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Firewall integration" (FortiGate configuration)

Prerequisite: An eXtended detection source reachable from the Jumpbox: FortiAnalyzer or FortiAnalyzer Cloud, FortiSIEM or FortiSIEM Cloud, Google Cloud Security Command Center with the Premium tier licensing that has Event Threat Detection, AWS GuardDuty, or a custom system
What it enables: Collecting activity logs from the source for eXtended detection
How to put it in place: Set up the source as the integration section describes; GUI: Profiles > Integrations > Connectors
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "eXtended detection source integration" (Prerequisites of each source)

Prerequisite: A STIX/TAXII threat intelligence server (TAXII (JSON) or TAXII 1 (XML)) with the collection to retrieve and an API key or credentials
What it enables: The Threat Intelligence Feed connector, which turns the collection into Threat Hunting queries
How to put it in place: Get the server address, collection ID, and credentials from the feed provider
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Threat Intelligence Feed integration"

Prerequisite: An Admin or IT user with the Custom script option
What it enables: Defining custom integration connectors and uploading actions in the Action Manager
How to put it in place: GUI: Administration > Users (Custom script)
Source: FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "Users" (Custom script) and "Custom integration"

Prerequisite: A back-end change by Fortinet Support
What it enables: The features that are enabled only through Fortinet Support: exceptions for specific command execution, the SSL connection between Collector and Core, and the Degraded Collector system event
How to put it in place: Open a Fortinet Support request for the change
Source: FortiEDR release notes (5.2.0 Core build 5.2.2.2027, 5.2.0 Central Manager build 3092, 6.0 Central Manager build 6.0.1.0940); FortiEDR 7.2.3 Administration Guide, "System events"
